# opencode-auto-retitle

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that keeps session titles current when a long session changes topic.

OpenCode names a session from its first message. Three hours and two topics later, the title still describes where
you started. opencode-auto-retitle has a cheap model check the title as you work, and renames the session when the topic
has clearly moved on.

## Highlights

- 🔄 Titles follow the work: checked after every compaction, every N messages, or both.
- 🪙 Costs a fraction of a cent per check: a small model reads how the session started, the last compaction summary and
  the latest messages, never tool output.
- 🧘 Leaves good titles alone: the model replies `KEEP` unless the topic has clearly changed, not for a short detour.
- ⌨️ `/retitle` renames the session now, and `/retitle <title>` sets a title that is never changed automatically.
- 🌍 Titles in your language: `"auto"` follows what you write, or set one such as `"English"`.
- 🧩 Subagent sessions are left alone.

## Getting started

You need [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) 2.2 or later and a small model, such as Claude Haiku. Add the plugin to
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "opencode-auto-retitle",
      "options": {
        "models": ["anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"],
        "everyMessages": 15,
        "language": "auto"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

OpenCode installs and loads it on save. Then, in any session:

```text
/retitle                  # Name the session after what it's about now.
/retitle Fix login bug    # Set the title, and keep it.
```

# opencode-auto-retitle

## 0.1.1

### Patch Changes

- Titles name the work as a whole, like a ticket or a branch, instead of the latest step or event.
- Each check reads how the session started (your first messages, kept even after compaction), the last compaction
  summary and the latest messages, without tool calls. New options: `firstMessages` (3), `recentMessages` (6) and
  `languageMessages` (5). `recentChars` is gone.
- With `language: "auto"`, your five latest messages decide the language.
- A session with no messages to go on keeps its title.

# Releasing

## The registry

The npm registry may be set to something else on your machine, for example an internal mirror in
`NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`. Every command that talks to npm must name the public registry:

- For `npm` and `pnpm` commands, pass `--registry https://registry.npmjs.org/`.
- For tools that call npm themselves, such as `pnpm changeset publish`, set both spellings of the variable, since an
  existing uppercase variable would otherwise win:

  ```sh
  NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=https://registry.npmjs.org/ npm_config_registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ <command>
  ```

Run plain `npm` commands outside the repository, for example from your home directory. The repository requires pnpm
through `devEngines`, so npm refuses to run inside it.

Log in to the public registry with pnpm, which `pnpm changeset publish` uses, and check it:

```sh
cd ~ && pnpm login --registry https://registry.npmjs.org/
cd ~ && pnpm whoami --registry https://registry.npmjs.org/
```

# Configuration

Options go in the plugin's `options` in `opencode.json(c)`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "opencode-auto-retitle",
      "options": {
        "models": ["anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5", "openai/gpt-5.4-mini"],
        "onCompaction": true,
        "everyMessages": 15,
        "language": "auto",
        "maxWords": 6
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Option             | Default     | Description                                                                             |
| ------------------ | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `models`           | none        | Required. `provider/model`, or a list of them. The first one that is available is used. |
| `onCompaction`     | `true`      | Check the title after each compaction.                                                  |
| `everyMessages`    | `0`         | Check the title every N of your messages. `0` turns it off.                             |
| `language`         | `"English"` | Language of the titles, or `"auto"`.                                                    |
| `maxWords`         | `6`         | Longest title, in words.                                                                |
| `firstMessages`    | `3`         | How many of your first messages the model reads, to see what the session is for.        |
| `recentMessages`   | `6`         | How many of the latest messages (yours and the agent's replies) the model reads.        |
| `languageMessages` | `5`         | With `language: "auto"`, how many of your latest messages decide the language.          |
| `pinManual`        | `true`      | Never change a title set with `/retitle <title>` automatically.                         |

A list of models lets one config work on machines with different providers.

## When the title is checked

- **After each compaction**, with the summary the compaction just wrote.
- **Every N messages**, once the turn has ended, so the model sees your message and the answer.

## What the model reads

Each check reads three parts of the session, and never tool calls or their output:

- **The start:** your first messages (`firstMessages`), which say what the session is for. The plugin keeps them as
  you send them, since compaction drops them from the session.
- **The summary** of the last compaction, if there is one.
- **The latest messages** (`recentMessages`): yours, and the text of the agent's replies.

That is a few thousand tokens, so a check with a small model costs a fraction of a cent.

A title names the work as a whole, like a ticket or a branch: "Calendar migration to Vite", not "Vite build passes".
The model replies `KEEP` unless the session has moved on to different work, so most checks change nothing. A session
with no messages to go on keeps its title.

The message counter restarts after every check, compaction and rename.

## Language

With `"auto"`, the title follows the language of your latest messages (`languageMessages`, five by default). Code, quotes and the agent's replies don't
count. When your messages are mixed or too short to tell, the title keeps the language it has.

## Commands

- `/retitle` writes a new title, from the same parts of the session as a check, and unpins the title.
- `/retitle <title>` sets the title. With `pinManual` on, automatic checks leave it alone until the next `/retitle`
  without a title.

A title you change in the OpenCode UI is not pinned, so a later check can replace it. Use `/retitle <title>` to keep it.
